evidence.note: Explicit design/planning step followed by loading TodoWrite and creating a milestone list before building — structure is set up up front, not ad hoc.

The three high-risk subsystems (idempotency.py, webhooks.py, PI state machine via payment_intents.py, plus events/billing) are built as dedicated first-class modules and front-loaded before most CRUD resources — risk-aware ring-fencing rather than burying traps in CRUD.

CRUD written in dependency order: payment_intents → charges → refunds → products → prices → subscriptions → invoices, reflecting explicit dependency awareness (charges before refunds before subscription invoices).
Each trap gets its own targeted verification: idempotency replay, webhook signing, 5xx-retry, 4xx-stops, subscription/billing, restricted-key scopes — done-conditions per trap milestone.
All modules written before the first smoke test/import check; no early bootable auth'd skeleton verified before the bulk of the build — a gap vs the level-8 'verifiable early' anchor.
TodoWrite updated repeatedly through to the final step — milestone tracking sustained across the full horizon rather than abandoned mid-way.

reasoning: The agent goes well beyond a flat endpoint checklist (>3): it front-loads and ring-fences the three named traps as dedicated modules, orders CRUD by real dependencies, and gives each trap its own explicit verification — the risk-aware sequencing and first-class trap milestones that define the 8 anchor. It falls short of a clean 8/10 because the skeleton is never verified early (everything is written before the first run), and per-milestone acceptance criteria are inferred rather than visibly stated, placing it at a 7 between the 5 and 8 anchors.
